title: Google now lets you make games with AI
content:
Google today announced Playground, a new browser-based platform for making custom games from AI prompts. Playground will be available today in the US for users who are 18 and older at playground.google.
Google now lets you make games with AI
Google Playground is a browser-based tool for making games from AI prompts.
The company is pitching it as an “experimental gaming platform” that “lowers the barriers to creation” and doesn’t require coding experience. “With Playground’s conversational interface, you can direct the game just by typing what you want to build,” Google says in a blog post. “Start from a blank canvas, remix starter prompts, or use guided support to shape your concept — and then test it right away. Want to tweak the physics, rewrite the rules, customize the characters, or overhaul the environment? Just ask. You stay in complete control of the creative direction from rough concept to final polish.”
When you’re finished making your game, you can share it with a link or publish it to the “Playground Explore gallery” so others can play it. “Select genres” will support in-game leaderboards and multiplayer. The gallery will highlight games that are “fresh, creative, and fun” using ratings and play activity, according to Google.
Playground is free to use, but if you have a Google One subscription, you’ll have higher weekly token limits based on your plan, Google spokesperson Nia Carter tells The Verge. Under the hood, Playground is powered by “Google’s existing foundation models (Gemini, Nano Banana, and Lyria) paired with a custom harness refined through our own internally built games and evaluations,” Carter says.
Alongside today’s Playground announcement, Google and Unity are also revealing Unity Spark, an AI game-making experience that’s closer to a professional-level game development engine and allows you to create games simultaneously with others. Games made with Unity Spark will be shareable on Playground. A closed beta for Spark is scheduled to kick off later this year, and people who are interested can get on a waitlist starting today.
Google’s news today follows Meta’s recent announcement that it will let users build games with AI on their phones and on the web for its Horizon platform with new apps rolling out in early access. Published games made with those tools will be able to be recommended on Facebook and Instagram, which could give them more reach than they would have just being on Horizon. Roblox has also started letting users make games with AI on their phones as part of a “Build” feature that’s in public alpha testing in a few countries.

report.summary: Google launched Playground, a browser-based AI tool that turns text prompts into shareable games, with Unity Spark for pro creators.
report.background: For years, game creation required engines like Unity, Unreal, or Godot and significant coding and design skill. Generative AI has begun changing that, letting users describe mechanics, assets, and rules in natural language. Google's Playground follows a broader race: Meta recently announced AI game creation for Horizon, Roblox is testing an AI 'Build' feature on phones, and startups offer prompt-to-game tools. Google is leveraging Gemini plus media models Nano Banana and Lyria, wrapped in a custom harness refined through internal games. The free, US-only, 18+ launch lowers entry barriers but also signals a strategic play: seed a new content ecosystem, drive Google One subscriptions through token limits, and position Google and Unity as infrastructure for AI-assisted game development. The result could be a surge of disposable, remixable games and new moderation, copyright, and quality challenges.
key_points: Playground is a free browser tool at playground.google, launching in the US for users 18 and older. It uses a conversational interface: start blank, remix prompts, or use guided support, then test immediately. Users can tweak physics, rules, characters, or environments by typing. Finished games can be shared via link or published to the Explore gallery. Google One subscribers get higher weekly token limits based on plan.

Under the hood, Playground combines Google foundation models: Gemini for reasoning and text, Nano Banana for image generation, and Lyria for music, paired with a custom harness refined via internal games and evaluations. This model mix suggests playable outputs, not just code snippets, with generated art, audio, and game logic. It also means quality and token costs depend on Google's cloud infrastructure.

Google and Unity announced Unity Spark, a more professional AI game-making experience. It supports simultaneous multiplayer creation and will publish games to Playground. A closed beta starts later this year, with a waitlist open now. Spark targets creators who want engine-level control, bridging no-code AI prototyping and traditional Unity development.

Playground enters a crowded field. Meta will let users build AI games for Horizon on phones and web, with recommendations on Facebook and Instagram; Roblox is testing AI 'Build' on phones. Google's differentiators are browser access, a Gemini model stack, an Explore gallery with ratings and play activity, and selected genres supporting leaderboards and multiplayer. Competition will test whether prompt-to-game tools produce lasting hits or novelty content.
report.impact: For the AI industry, Playground is a showcase for multimodal foundation models as creative engines, not just chatbots, pushing Gemini, Nano Banana, and Lyria into interactive entertainment. It validates a shift from AI-assisted coding to AI-generated experiences, likely accelerating investment in agentic game design and real-time generation. For developers, low-cost prototyping and remixing could speed ideation, but also commoditize simple genres and raise questions about IP, attribution, and platform lock-in. Unity Spark may create a hybrid path: AI drafts, pros polish. For regular users, making a game becomes as easy as chatting, potentially flooding stores with remixable microgames. Expect moderation, copyright, and discoverability hurdles, plus new opportunities for hobbyists, educators, and streamers.
report.tools: To follow this space: try Google Playground in the US if 18 or older, and join the Unity Spark waitlist. Watch Meta Horizon AI creation tools and Roblox's Build alpha. For open-source or developer-friendly paths, explore Godot, Phaser, LOVE, and Twine for prototyping, plus AI asset tools like Stable Diffusion, Suno, and Ludo.ai. Also track Gemini, Nano Banana, and Lyria APIs as they open up.
